Beyond the established facts, researchers are actively testing several candidate mechanisms, none of them conclusively proven. Viral RNA has been detected in blood months after acute infection in some patients, though whether that persisting material actually drives symptoms is unsettled, and one placebo-controlled antiviral trial found no significant benefit. Studies show abnormal immune activation and signs of dormant Epstein-Barr virus reactivating. Many patients show autonomic nervous system problems, including postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. Others show signs their cells aren't producing energy efficiently, and altered gut bacteria at hospital admission has been shown to predict long COVID status six months later. Each of these is a plausible contributor; none of them alone explains the whole picture.
